prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: ONE standalone square transparent mineral-overlay master for reduction to a 16x16 Minecraft ore-block texture.
Primary request: Coal Measures, variant 2, RICHER deposit role. One modest horizontal broken coal bench occupies one local zone, with a small offset fragment lower down. It ends within the face; broad clear rock gaps interrupt it. Geology: sedimentary coal benches split by siltstone partings. This block is only an incidental small window into a larger deposit; the deposit identity appears across a tiled patch, not on this individual face.
Scene/backdrop: genuine transparent RGBA; all space outside actual mineral clusters has alpha zero. No rendered stone, deepslate, matte, checkerboard or scene.
Style/medium: intentional Minecraft Java 16x16-style square pixel clusters drawn at high resolution, hard crisp stepped edges, a few flat medium values, no soft painting or antialiasing.
Composition/framing: LOCALLY richer but still modest: target 25–45 materially visible pixels of 256 after reduction, about 10–18% of the face. Only one partial main exposure and at most one sparse associated trace. Vast clear alpha remains. Do not compose a complete ore specimen or a fully explained geology illustration inside this block.
Materials/textures: matte medium charcoal coal, close to dark stone, a small dull gray-brown silt parting; no jet black or pale rail. Mostly opaque mineral cluster pixels, medium local values close to stone; no blanket opacity fade, no bright or dark outlining, no highlight rails or raised/carved relief.
Constraints: exactly one 1:1 square PNG at least 1024x1024 with real transparent alpha; one overlay only; no host pixels; no frame, panel, text, label or watermark.
Avoid: Black Shale's steep hairline cleavage, glossy black bars, broad repeated seams; whole-face composition, multiple complete structures, decorative speckles, drawn checkerboard, colored or gray backdrop, haze, vignette, shadow, glow, gradients, smooth painting, photorealism.
disposition: Retained unchanged as first pattern within category; active human review
